<ns0:uscDoc xmlns:ns0="http://xml.house.gov/schemas/uslm/1.0" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xsi:schemaLocation="http://xml.house.gov/schemas/uslm/1.0 USLM-1.0.15.xsd" xml:lang="en" identifier="/us/usc/t15"><ns0:subsection style="-uslm-lc:I19" class="indent2 firstIndent-2" id="id6c7bdad7-86b3-11f1-8c1e-ca5e0ea6b57b" identifier="/us/usc/t15/s9009a/d"><ns0:num value="d" class="bold">(d)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Use of funds</ns0:heading><ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I79" class="indent3 firstIndent-2" id="id6c7bdad8-86b3-11f1-8c1e-ca5e0ea6b57b" identifier="/us/usc/t15/s9009a/d/1"><ns0:num value="1" class="bold">(1)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Timing</ns0:heading><ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I18" class="indent4 firstIndent-2" id="id6c7bdad9-86b3-11f1-8c1e-ca5e0ea6b57b" identifier="/us/usc/t15/s9009a/d/1/A"><ns0:num value="A" class="bold">(A)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Expenses incurred</ns0:heading><ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I77" class="indent5 firstIndent-2" id="id6c7bdada-86b3-11f1-8c1e-ca5e0ea6b57b" identifier="/us/usc/t15/s9009a/d/1/A/i"><ns0:num value="i" class="bold">(i)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> In general</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I14" class="indent3">Except as provided in clause (ii), amounts received under a grant under this section may be used for costs incurred during the period beginning on <ns0:date date="2020-03-01">March 1, 2020</ns0:date>, and ending on <ns0:date date="2021-12-31">December 31, 2021</ns0:date>.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:clause>
<ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I77" class="indent5 firstIndent-2" id="id6c7bdadb-86b3-11f1-8c1e-ca5e0ea6b57b" identifier="/us/usc/t15/s9009a/d/1/A/ii"><ns0:num value="ii" class="bold">(ii)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Extension for supplemental grants</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I14" class="indent3">If an eligible person or entity receives a grant under subsection (b)(3), amounts received under either grant under this section may be used for costs incurred during the period beginning on <ns0:date date="2020-03-01">March 1, 2020</ns0:date>, and ending on <ns0:date date="2022-06-30">June 30, 2022</ns0:date>.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:clause>
</ns0:subparagraph>
<ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I18" class="indent4 firstIndent-2" id="id6c7bdadc-86b3-11f1-8c1e-ca5e0ea6b57b" identifier="/us/usc/t15/s9009a/d/1/B"><ns0:num value="B" class="bold">(B)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Expenditure</ns0:heading><ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I77" class="indent5 firstIndent-2" id="id6c7bdadd-86b3-11f1-8c1e-ca5e0ea6b57b" identifier="/us/usc/t15/s9009a/d/1/B/i"><ns0:num value="i" class="bold">(i)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> In general</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I14" class="indent3">Except as provided in clause (ii), an eligible person or entity shall return to the Administrator any amounts received under a grant under this section that are not expended on or before the date that is 1 year after the date of disbursement of the grant.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:clause>
<ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I77" class="indent5 firstIndent-2" id="id6c7bdade-86b3-11f1-8c1e-ca5e0ea6b57b" identifier="/us/usc/t15/s9009a/d/1/B/ii"><ns0:num value="ii" class="bold">(ii)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Extension for supplemental grants</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I14" class="indent3">If an eligible person or entity receives a grant under subsection (b)(3), the eligible person or entity shall return to the Administrator any amounts received under either grant under this section that are not expended on or before the date that is 18 months after the date of disbursement to the eligible person or entity of the grant under subsection (b)(2).</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:clause>
</ns0:subparagraph>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I79" class="indent3 firstIndent-2" id="id6c7bdadf-86b3-11f1-8c1e-ca5e0ea6b57b" identifier="/us/usc/t15/s9009a/d/2"><ns0:num value="2" class="bold">(2)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Allowable expenses</ns0:heading><ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I18" class="indent4 firstIndent-2" id="id6c7bdae0-86b3-11f1-8c1e-ca5e0ea6b57b" identifier="/us/usc/t15/s9009a/d/2/A"><ns0:num value="A" class="bold">(A)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Definitions</ns0:heading><ns0:chapeau style="-uslm-lc:I13" class="indent2">In this paragraph—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I14" class="indent3" id="id6c7bdae1-86b3-11f1-8c1e-ca5e0ea6b57b" identifier="/us/usc/t15/s9009a/d/2/A/i"><ns0:num value="i">(i)</ns0:num><ns0:content> the terms “covered mortgage obligation”, “covered rent obligation”, “covered utility payment”, and “covered worker protection expenditure” have the meanings given those terms in <ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t15/s636m/a">section 636m(a) of this title</ns0:ref>, as redesignated, transferred, and amended by this Act; and</ns0:content>
</ns0:clause>
<ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I14" class="indent3" id="id6c7bdae2-86b3-11f1-8c1e-ca5e0ea6b57b" identifier="/us/usc/t15/s9009a/d/2/A/ii"><ns0:num value="ii">(ii)</ns0:num><ns0:content> the term “payroll costs” has the meaning given that term in <ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t15/s636/a/36/A">section 636(a)(36)(A) of this title</ns0:ref>.</ns0:content>
</ns0:clause>
</ns0:subparagraph>
<ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I18" class="indent4 firstIndent-2" id="id6c7bdae3-86b3-11f1-8c1e-ca5e0ea6b57b" identifier="/us/usc/t15/s9009a/d/2/B"><ns0:num value="B" class="bold">(B)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Expenses</ns0:heading><ns0:chapeau style="-uslm-lc:I13" class="indent2">An eligible person or entity may use amounts received under a grant under this section for—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I14" class="indent3" id="id6c7bdae4-86b3-11f1-8c1e-ca5e0ea6b57b" identifier="/us/usc/t15/s9009a/d/2/B/i"><ns0:num value="i">(i)</ns0:num><ns0:content> payroll costs;</ns0:content>
</ns0:clause>
<ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I14" class="indent3" id="id6c7bdae5-86b3-11f1-8c1e-ca5e0ea6b57b" identifier="/us/usc/t15/s9009a/d/2/B/ii"><ns0:num value="ii">(ii)</ns0:num><ns0:content> payments on any covered rent obligation;</ns0:content>
</ns0:clause>
<ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I14" class="indent3" id="id6c7bdae6-86b3-11f1-8c1e-ca5e0ea6b57b" identifier="/us/usc/t15/s9009a/d/2/B/iii"><ns0:num value="iii">(iii)</ns0:num><ns0:content> any covered utility payment;</ns0:content>
</ns0:clause>
<ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I14" class="indent3" id="id6c7bdae7-86b3-11f1-8c1e-ca5e0ea6b57b" identifier="/us/usc/t15/s9009a/d/2/B/iv"><ns0:num value="iv">(iv)</ns0:num><ns0:content> scheduled payments of interest or principal on any covered mortgage obligation (which shall not include any prepayment of principal on a covered mortgage obligation);</ns0:content>
</ns0:clause>
<ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I14" class="indent3" id="id6c7bdae8-86b3-11f1-8c1e-ca5e0ea6b57b" identifier="/us/usc/t15/s9009a/d/2/B/v"><ns0:num value="v">(v)</ns0:num><ns0:content> scheduled payments of interest or principal on any indebtedness or debt instrument (which shall not include any prepayment of principal) incurred in the ordinary course of business that is a liability of the eligible person or entity and was incurred prior to <ns0:date date="2020-02-15">February 15, 2020</ns0:date>;</ns0:content>
</ns0:clause>
<ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I14" class="indent3" id="id6c7bdae9-86b3-11f1-8c1e-ca5e0ea6b57b" identifier="/us/usc/t15/s9009a/d/2/B/vi"><ns0:num value="vi">(vi)</ns0:num><ns0:content> covered worker protection expenditures;</ns0:content>
</ns0:clause>
<ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I14" class="indent3" id="id6c7bdaea-86b3-11f1-8c1e-ca5e0ea6b57b" identifier="/us/usc/t15/s9009a/d/2/B/vii"><ns0:num value="vii">(vii)</ns0:num><ns0:content> payments made to independent contractors, as reported on Form–1099 MISC, not to exceed a total of $100,000 in annual compensation for any individual employee of an independent contractor; and</ns0:content>
</ns0:clause>
<ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I14" class="indent3" id="id6c7bdaeb-86b3-11f1-8c1e-ca5e0ea6b57b" identifier="/us/usc/t15/s9009a/d/2/B/viii"><ns0:num value="viii">(viii)</ns0:num><ns0:chapeau> other ordinary and necessary business expenses, including—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4" id="id6c7bdaec-86b3-11f1-8c1e-ca5e0ea6b57b" identifier="/us/usc/t15/s9009a/d/2/B/viii/I"><ns0:num value="I">(I)</ns0:num><ns0:content> maintenance expenses;</ns0:content>
</ns0:subclause>
<ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4" id="id6c7bdaed-86b3-11f1-8c1e-ca5e0ea6b57b" identifier="/us/usc/t15/s9009a/d/2/B/viii/II"><ns0:num value="II">(II)</ns0:num><ns0:content> administrative costs, including fees and licensing costs;</ns0:content>
</ns0:subclause>
<ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4" id="id6c7bdaee-86b3-11f1-8c1e-ca5e0ea6b57b" identifier="/us/usc/t15/s9009a/d/2/B/viii/III"><ns0:num value="III">(III)</ns0:num><ns0:content> State and local taxes and fees;</ns0:content>
</ns0:subclause>
<ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4" id="id6c7bdaef-86b3-11f1-8c1e-ca5e0ea6b57b" identifier="/us/usc/t15/s9009a/d/2/B/viii/IV"><ns0:num value="IV">(IV)</ns0:num><ns0:content> operating leases in effect as of <ns0:date date="2020-02-15">February 15, 2020</ns0:date>;</ns0:content>
</ns0:subclause>
<ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4" id="id6c7bdaf0-86b3-11f1-8c1e-ca5e0ea6b57b" identifier="/us/usc/t15/s9009a/d/2/B/viii/V"><ns0:num value="V">(V)</ns0:num><ns0:content> payments required for insurance on any insurance policy; and</ns0:content>
</ns0:subclause>
<ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4" id="id6c7bdaf1-86b3-11f1-8c1e-ca5e0ea6b57b" identifier="/us/usc/t15/s9009a/d/2/B/viii/VI"><ns0:num value="VI">(VI)</ns0:num><ns0:content> advertising, production transportation, and capital expenditures related to producing a theatrical or live performing arts production, concert, exhibition, or comedy show, except that a grant under this section may not be used primarily for such expenditures.</ns0:content>
</ns0:subclause>
</ns0:clause>
</ns0:subparagraph>
</ns0:paragraph>
<ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I79" class="indent3 firstIndent-2" id="id6c7bdaf2-86b3-11f1-8c1e-ca5e0ea6b57b" identifier="/us/usc/t15/s9009a/d/3"><ns0:num value="3" class="bold">(3)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Prohibited expenses</ns0:heading><ns0:chapeau style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1">An eligible person or entity may not use amounts received under a grant under this section—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I13" class="indent2" id="id6c7bdaf3-86b3-11f1-8c1e-ca5e0ea6b57b" identifier="/us/usc/t15/s9009a/d/3/A"><ns0:num value="A">(A)</ns0:num><ns0:content> to purchase real estate;</ns0:content>
</ns0:subparagraph>
<ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I13" class="indent2" id="id6c7bdaf4-86b3-11f1-8c1e-ca5e0ea6b57b" identifier="/us/usc/t15/s9009a/d/3/B"><ns0:num value="B">(B)</ns0:num><ns0:content> for payments of interest or principal on loans originated after <ns0:date date="2020-02-15">February 15, 2020</ns0:date>;</ns0:content>
</ns0:subparagraph>
<ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I13" class="indent2" id="id6c7bdaf5-86b3-11f1-8c1e-ca5e0ea6b57b" identifier="/us/usc/t15/s9009a/d/3/C"><ns0:num value="C">(C)</ns0:num><ns0:content> to invest or re-lend funds;</ns0:content>
</ns0:subparagraph>
<ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I13" class="indent2" id="id6c7bdaf6-86b3-11f1-8c1e-ca5e0ea6b57b" identifier="/us/usc/t15/s9009a/d/3/D"><ns0:num value="D">(D)</ns0:num><ns0:content> for contributions or expenditures to, or on behalf of, any political party, party committee, or candidate for elective office; or</ns0:content>
</ns0:subparagraph>
<ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I13" class="indent2" id="id6c7bdaf7-86b3-11f1-8c1e-ca5e0ea6b57b" identifier="/us/usc/t15/s9009a/d/3/E"><ns0:num value="E">(E)</ns0:num><ns0:content> for any other use as may be prohibited by the Administrator.</ns0:content>
</ns0:subparagraph>
</ns0:paragraph>
</ns0:subsection>
</ns0:uscDoc>

document.text:
(1) Election to maintain balances

(A) Prefunding balance

The plan sponsor of a single-employer plan may elect to maintain a prefunding balance.


(B) Funding standard carryover balance

(i) In general

In the case of a single-employer plan described in clause (ii), the plan sponsor may elect to maintain a funding standard carryover balance, until such balance is reduced to zero.


(ii) Plans maintaining funding standard account in 2007 A plan is described in this clause if the plan—

(I) was in effect for a plan year beginning in 2007, and

(II) had a positive balance in the funding standard account under section 1082(b) of this title as in effect for such plan year and determined as of the end of such plan year.

(16) Credit for certain small business concern subcontractors.—

(A) In general.— For purposes of determining whether or not a prime contractor has attained the percentage goals specified in paragraph (6)—

(i) if the subcontracting goals pertain only to a single contract with a Federal agency, the prime contractor may elect to receive credit for small business concerns performing as first tier subcontractors or subcontractors at any tier pursuant to the subcontracting plans required under paragraph (6)(D) in an amount equal to the total dollar value of any subcontracts awarded to such small business concerns; and

(ii) if the subcontracting goals pertain to more than one contract with one or more Federal agencies, or to one contract with more than one Federal agency, the prime contractor may only receive credit for first tier subcontractors that are small business concerns.


(B) Collection and review of data on subcontracting plans.— The head of each contracting agency shall ensure that the agency—

(i) collects and reports data on the extent to which prime contractors of the agency meet the goals and objectives set forth in subcontracting plans submitted pursuant to this subsection; and

(ii) periodically reviews data collected and reported pursuant to clause (i) for the purpose of ensuring that such contractors comply in good faith with the requirements of this subsection.


(C) Rule of construction.— Nothing in this paragraph shall be construed to allow a Federal agency to establish a goal for an 5

5 So in original. Probably should be “a”.

 number of subcontracts with a subcontractor at any tier for a prime contractor otherwise eligible to receive credit under this paragraph.

<ns0:uscDoc xmlns:ns0="http://xml.house.gov/schemas/uslm/1.0" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xsi:schemaLocation="http://xml.house.gov/schemas/uslm/1.0 USLM-1.0.15.xsd" xml:lang="en" identifier="/us/usc/t20"><ns0:paragraph style="-uslm-lc:I79" class="indent3 firstIndent-2" id="id0da39bf5-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1"><ns0:num value="1" class="bold">(1)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Definitions</ns0:heading><ns0:chapeau style="-uslm-lc:I12" class="indent1">In this chapter:</ns0:chapeau><ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I18" class="indent4 firstIndent-2" id="id0da39bf6-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A"><ns0:num value="A" class="bold">(A)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Individualized education program</ns0:heading><ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I77" class="indent5 firstIndent-2" id="id0da39bf7-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/i"><ns0:num value="i" class="bold">(i)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> In general</ns0:heading><ns0:chapeau style="-uslm-lc:I14" class="indent3">The term “individualized education program” or “IEP” means a written statement for each child with a disability that is developed, reviewed, and revised in accordance with this section and that includes—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4" id="id0da39bf8-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/i/I"><ns0:num value="I">(I)</ns0:num><ns0:chapeau> a statement of the child’s present levels of academic achievement and functional performance, including—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:item style="-uslm-lc:I580434" class="indent5" id="id0da39bf9-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/i/I/aa"><ns0:num value="aa">(aa)</ns0:num><ns0:content> how the child’s disability affects the child’s involvement and progress in the general education curriculum;</ns0:content>
</ns0:item>
<ns0:item style="-uslm-lc:I580434" class="indent5" id="id0da39bfa-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/i/I/bb"><ns0:num value="bb">(bb)</ns0:num><ns0:content> for preschool children, as appropriate, how the disability affects the child’s participation in appropriate activities; and</ns0:content>
</ns0:item>
<ns0:item style="-uslm-lc:I580434" class="indent5" id="id0da39bfb-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/i/I/cc"><ns0:num value="cc">(cc)</ns0:num><ns0:content> for children with disabilities who take alternate assessments aligned to alternate achievement standards, a description of benchmarks or short-term objectives;</ns0:content>
</ns0:item>
</ns0:subclause>
<ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4" id="id0da39bfc-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/i/II"><ns0:num value="II">(II)</ns0:num><ns0:chapeau> a statement of measurable annual goals, including academic and functional goals, designed to—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:item style="-uslm-lc:I580434" class="indent5" id="id0da39bfd-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/i/II/aa"><ns0:num value="aa">(aa)</ns0:num><ns0:content> meet the child’s needs that result from the child’s disability to enable the child to be involved in and make progress in the general education curriculum; and</ns0:content>
</ns0:item>
<ns0:item style="-uslm-lc:I580434" class="indent5" id="id0da39bfe-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/i/II/bb"><ns0:num value="bb">(bb)</ns0:num><ns0:content> meet each of the child’s other educational needs that result from the child’s disability;</ns0:content>
</ns0:item>
</ns0:subclause>
<ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4" id="id0da39bff-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/i/III"><ns0:num value="III">(III)</ns0:num><ns0:content> a description of how the child’s progress toward meeting the annual goals described in subclause (II) will be measured and when periodic reports on the progress the child is making toward meeting the annual goals (such as through the use of quarterly or other periodic reports, concurrent with the issuance of report cards) will be provided;</ns0:content>
</ns0:subclause>
<ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4" id="id0da39c00-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/i/IV"><ns0:num value="IV">(IV)</ns0:num><ns0:chapeau> a statement of the special education and related services and supplementary aids and services, based on peer-reviewed research to the extent practicable, to be provided to the child, or on behalf of the child, and a statement of the program modifications or supports for school personnel that will be provided for the child—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:item style="-uslm-lc:I580434" class="indent5" id="id0da39c01-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/i/IV/aa"><ns0:num value="aa">(aa)</ns0:num><ns0:content> to advance appropriately toward attaining the annual goals;</ns0:content>
</ns0:item>
<ns0:item style="-uslm-lc:I580434" class="indent5" id="id0da39c02-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/i/IV/bb"><ns0:num value="bb">(bb)</ns0:num><ns0:content> to be involved in and make progress in the general education curriculum in accordance with subclause (I) and to participate in extracurricular and other nonacademic activities; and</ns0:content>
</ns0:item>
<ns0:item style="-uslm-lc:I580434" class="indent5" id="id0da39c03-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/i/IV/cc"><ns0:num value="cc">(cc)</ns0:num><ns0:content> to be educated and participate with other children with disabilities and nondisabled children in the activities described in this subparagraph;</ns0:content>
</ns0:item>
</ns0:subclause>
<ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4" id="id0da39c04-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/i/V"><ns0:num value="V">(V)</ns0:num><ns0:content> an explanation of the extent, if any, to which the child will not participate with nondisabled children in the regular class and in the activities described in subclause (IV)(cc);</ns0:content>
</ns0:subclause>
<ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4" id="id0da39c05-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/i/VI"><ns0:num value="VI">(VI)</ns0:num><ns0:item style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4" id="id0da39c06-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/i/VI/aa"><ns0:num value="aa">(aa)</ns0:num><ns0:content> a statement of any individual appropriate accommodations that are necessary to measure the academic achievement and functional performance of the child on State and districtwide assessments consistent with <ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t20/s1412/a/16/A">section 1412(a)(16)(A) of this title</ns0:ref>; and</ns0:content>
</ns0:item>
<ns0:item style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4" id="id0da39c07-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/i/VI/bb"><ns0:num value="bb">(bb)</ns0:num><ns0:chapeau> if the IEP Team determines that the child shall take an alternate assessment on a particular State or districtwide assessment of student achievement, a statement of why—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:subitem style="-uslm-lc:I580434" class="indent5" id="id0da39c08-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/i/VI/bb/AA"><ns0:num value="AA">(AA)</ns0:num><ns0:content> the child cannot participate in the regular assessment; and</ns0:content>
</ns0:subitem>
<ns0:subitem style="-uslm-lc:I580434" class="indent5" id="id0da39c09-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/i/VI/bb/BB"><ns0:num value="BB">(BB)</ns0:num><ns0:content> the particular alternate assessment selected is appropriate for the child;</ns0:content>
</ns0:subitem>
</ns0:item>
</ns0:subclause>
<ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4" id="id0da39c0a-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/i/VII"><ns0:num value="VII">(VII)</ns0:num><ns0:content> the projected date for the beginning of the services and modifications described in subclause (IV), and the anticipated frequency, location, and duration of those services and modifications; and</ns0:content>
</ns0:subclause>
<ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4" id="id0da39c0b-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/i/VIII"><ns0:num value="VIII">(VIII)</ns0:num><ns0:chapeau> beginning not later than the first IEP to be in effect when the child is 16, and updated annually thereafter—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:item style="-uslm-lc:I580434" class="indent5" id="id0da39c0c-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/i/VIII/aa"><ns0:num value="aa">(aa)</ns0:num><ns0:content> appropriate measurable postsecondary goals based upon age appropriate transition assessments related to training, education, employment, and, where appropriate, independent living skills;</ns0:content>
</ns0:item>
<ns0:item style="-uslm-lc:I580434" class="indent5" id="id0da39c0d-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/i/VIII/bb"><ns0:num value="bb">(bb)</ns0:num><ns0:content> the transition services (including courses of study) needed to assist the child in reaching those goals; and</ns0:content>
</ns0:item>
<ns0:item style="-uslm-lc:I580434" class="indent5" id="id0da39c0e-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/i/VIII/cc"><ns0:num value="cc">(cc)</ns0:num><ns0:content> beginning not later than 1 year before the child reaches the age of majority under State law, a statement that the child has been informed of the child’s rights under this chapter, if any, that will transfer to the child on reaching the age of majority under <ns0:ref href="/us/usc/t20/s1415/m">section 1415(m) of this title</ns0:ref>.</ns0:content>
</ns0:item>
</ns0:subclause>
</ns0:clause>
<ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I77" class="indent5 firstIndent-2" id="id0da39c0f-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/ii"><ns0:num value="ii" class="bold">(ii)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Rule of construction</ns0:heading><ns0:chapeau style="-uslm-lc:I14" class="indent3">Nothing in this section shall be construed to require—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4" id="id0da39c10-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/ii/I"><ns0:num value="I">(I)</ns0:num><ns0:content> that additional information be included in a child’s IEP beyond what is explicitly required in this section; and</ns0:content>
</ns0:subclause>
<ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4" id="id0da39c11-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/A/ii/II"><ns0:num value="II">(II)</ns0:num><ns0:content> the IEP Team to include information under 1 component of a child’s IEP that is already contained under another component of such IEP.</ns0:content>
</ns0:subclause>
</ns0:clause>
</ns0:subparagraph>
<ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I18" class="indent4 firstIndent-2" id="id0da39c12-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/B"><ns0:num value="B" class="bold">(B)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Individualized education program team</ns0:heading><ns0:chapeau style="-uslm-lc:I13" class="indent2">The term “individualized education program team” or “IEP Team” means a group of individuals composed of—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I14" class="indent3" id="id0da39c13-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/B/i"><ns0:num value="i">(i)</ns0:num><ns0:content> the parents of a child with a disability;</ns0:content>
</ns0:clause>
<ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I14" class="indent3" id="id0da39c14-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/B/ii"><ns0:num value="ii">(ii)</ns0:num><ns0:content> not less than 1 regular education teacher of such child (if the child is, or may be, participating in the regular education environment);</ns0:content>
</ns0:clause>
<ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I14" class="indent3" id="id0da39c15-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/B/iii"><ns0:num value="iii">(iii)</ns0:num><ns0:content> not less than 1 special education teacher, or where appropriate, not less than 1 special education provider of such child;</ns0:content>
</ns0:clause>
<ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I14" class="indent3" id="id0da39c16-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/B/iv"><ns0:num value="iv">(iv)</ns0:num><ns0:chapeau> a representative of the local educational agency who—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4" id="id0da39c17-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/B/iv/I"><ns0:num value="I">(I)</ns0:num><ns0:content> is qualified to provide, or supervise the provision of, specially designed instruction to meet the unique needs of children with disabilities;</ns0:content>
</ns0:subclause>
<ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4" id="id0da39c18-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/B/iv/II"><ns0:num value="II">(II)</ns0:num><ns0:content> is knowledgeable about the general education curriculum; and</ns0:content>
</ns0:subclause>
<ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4" id="id0da39c19-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/B/iv/III"><ns0:num value="III">(III)</ns0:num><ns0:content> is knowledgeable about the availability of resources of the local educational agency;</ns0:content>
</ns0:subclause>
</ns0:clause>
<ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I14" class="indent3" id="id0da39c1a-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/B/v"><ns0:num value="v">(v)</ns0:num><ns0:content> an individual who can interpret the instructional implications of evaluation results, who may be a member of the team described in clauses (ii) through (vi);</ns0:content>
</ns0:clause>
<ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I14" class="indent3" id="id0da39c1b-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/B/vi"><ns0:num value="vi">(vi)</ns0:num><ns0:content> at the discretion of the parent or the agency, other individuals who have knowledge or special expertise regarding the child, including related services personnel as appropriate; and</ns0:content>
</ns0:clause>
<ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I14" class="indent3" id="id0da39c1c-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/B/vii"><ns0:num value="vii">(vii)</ns0:num><ns0:content> whenever appropriate, the child with a disability.</ns0:content>
</ns0:clause>
</ns0:subparagraph>
<ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I18" class="indent4 firstIndent-2" id="id0da39c1d-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/C"><ns0:num value="C" class="bold">(C)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> IEP Team attendance</ns0:heading><ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I77" class="indent5 firstIndent-2" id="id0da39c1e-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/C/i"><ns0:num value="i" class="bold">(i)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Attendance not necessary</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I14" class="indent3">A member of the IEP Team shall not be required to attend an IEP meeting, in whole or in part, if the parent of a child with a disability and the local educational agency agree that the attendance of such member is not necessary because the member’s area of the curriculum or related services is not being modified or discussed in the meeting.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:clause>
<ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I77" class="indent5 firstIndent-2" id="id0da39c1f-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/C/ii"><ns0:num value="ii" class="bold">(ii)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Excusal</ns0:heading><ns0:chapeau style="-uslm-lc:I14" class="indent3">A member of the IEP Team may be excused from attending an IEP meeting, in whole or in part, when the meeting involves a modification to or discussion of the member’s area of the curriculum or related services, if—</ns0:chapeau><ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4" id="id0da39c20-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/C/ii/I"><ns0:num value="I">(I)</ns0:num><ns0:content> the parent and the local educational agency consent to the excusal; and</ns0:content>
</ns0:subclause>
<ns0:subclause style="-uslm-lc:I16" class="indent4" id="id0da39c21-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/C/ii/II"><ns0:num value="II">(II)</ns0:num><ns0:content> the member submits, in writing to the parent and the IEP Team, input into the development of the IEP prior to the meeting.</ns0:content>
</ns0:subclause>
</ns0:clause>
<ns0:clause style="-uslm-lc:I77" class="indent5 firstIndent-2" id="id0da39c22-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/C/iii"><ns0:num value="iii" class="bold">(iii)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> Written agreement and consent required</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I14" class="indent3">A parent’s agreement under clause (i) and consent under clause (ii) shall be in writing.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:clause>
</ns0:subparagraph>
<ns0:subparagraph style="-uslm-lc:I18" class="indent4 firstIndent-2" id="id0da39c23-3a70-11f1-a648-bee82ed8a795" identifier="/us/usc/t20/s1414/d/1/D"><ns0:num value="D" class="bold">(D)</ns0:num><ns0:heading class="bold"> IEP Team transition</ns0:heading><ns0:content><ns0:p style="-uslm-lc:I13" class="indent2">In the case of a child who was previously served under subchapter III, an invitation to the initial IEP meeting shall, at the request of the parent, be sent to the subchapter III service coordinator or other representatives of the subchapter III system to assist with the smooth transition of services.</ns0:p>
</ns0:content>
</ns0:subparagraph>
</ns0:paragraph>
</ns0:uscDoc>

accepted.summary: In this chapter, the term “individualized education program” or “IEP” means a written statement for each child with a disability that is developed, reviewed, and revised in accordance with this section and that includes: (I) a statement of the child’s present levels of academic achievement and functional performance (including how the child’s disability affects involvement and progress in the general education curriculum, for preschool children as appropriate how it affects participation in appropriate activities, and for children with disabilities who take alternate assessments aligned to alternate achievement standards, a description of benchmarks or short-term objectives); (II) a statement of measurable annual goals, including academic and functional goals, designed to meet the child’s needs resulting from the disability to enable involvement and progress in the general education curriculum and meet each of the child's other educational needs resulting from the disability; (III) a description of how progress toward meeting the annual goals will be measured and when periodic reports on progress (such as quarterly or other periodic reports concurrent with report cards) will be provided; (IV) a statement of the special education, related services, and supplementary aids and services based on peer-reviewed research to the extent practicable, and program modifications or supports for school personnel to be provided for the child to advance appropriately toward attaining annual goals, be involved and progress in the general education curriculum, participate in extracurricular and nonacademic activities, and be educated and participate with other disabled and nondisabled children; (V) an explanation of the extent, if any, to which the child will not participate with nondisabled children in the regular class and activities; (VI) a statement of any individual appropriate accommodations necessary to measure academic achievement and functional performance on State and districtwide assessments consistent with section 1412(a)(16)(A), and if the IEP Team determines the child shall take an alternate assessment on a particular State or districtwide assessment of student achievement, a statement of why the child cannot participate in the regular assessment and why the particular alternate assessment selected is appropriate; (VII) the projected date for the beginning of services and modifications, and their anticipated frequency, location, and duration; and (VIII) beginning not later than the first IEP to be in effect when the child is 16 and updated annually thereafter, appropriate measurable postsecondary goals based upon age-appropriate transition assessments related to training, education, employment, and where appropriate independent living skills, and transition services needed to assist the child in reaching those goals, as well as beginning not later than 1 year before reaching the age of majority under State law, a statement that the child has been informed of the rights under this chapter, if any, that will transfer to the child on reaching the age of majority under section 1415(m).

evidence.quote: (i) In general

The term “individualized education program” or “IEP” means a written statement for each child with a disability that is developed, reviewed, and revised in accordance with this section and that includes—
(I) a statement of the child’s present levels of academic achievement and functional performance, including—

(aa) a statement of any individual appropriate accommodations that are necessary to measure the academic achievement and functional performance of the child on State and districtwide assessments consistent with section 1412(a)(16)(A) of this title; and

(bb) if the IEP Team determines that the child shall take an alternate assessment on a particular State or districtwide assessment of student achievement, a statement of why—

(AA) the child cannot participate in the regular assessment; and

(BB) the particular alternate assessment selected is appropriate for the child;



(VII) the projected date for the beginning of the services and modifications described in subclause (IV), and the anticipated frequency, location, and duration of those services and modifications; and

(VIII) beginning not later than the first IEP to be in effect when the child is 16, and updated annually thereafter—
(i) In general

The term “individualized education program” or “IEP” means a written statement for each child with a disability that is developed, reviewed, and revised in accordance with this section and that includes—
(I) a statement of the child’s present levels of academic achievement and functional performance, including—

(aa) a statement of any individual appropriate accommodations that are necessary to measure the academic achievement and functional performance of the child on State and districtwide assessments consistent with section 1412(a)(16)(A) of this title; and

(bb) if the IEP Team determines that the child shall take an alternate assessment on a particular State or districtwide assessment of student achievement, a statement of why—

(AA) the child cannot participate in the regular assessment; and

(BB) the particular alternate assessment selected is appropriate for the child;



(VII) the projected date for the beginning of the services and modifications described in subclause (IV), and the anticipated frequency, location, and duration of those services and modifications; and

(VIII) beginning not later than the first IEP to be in effect when the child is 16, and updated annually thereafter—
(1) Definitions
In this chapter:

rkaf:assertsValue.@value: In this chapter, the term “individualized education program” or “IEP” means a written statement for each child with a disability that is developed, reviewed, and revised in accordance with this section and that includes: (I) a statement of the child’s present levels of academic achievement and functional performance (including how the child’s disability affects involvement and progress in the general education curriculum, for preschool children as appropriate how it affects participation in appropriate activities, and for children with disabilities who take alternate assessments aligned to alternate achievement standards, a description of benchmarks or short-term objectives); (III) a description of how progress toward meeting the annual goals will be measured and when periodic reports on progress (such as quarterly or other periodic reports concurrent with report cards) will be provided; (IV) a statement of the special education, related services, and supplementary aids and services based on peer-reviewed research to the extent practicable, and program modifications or supports for school personnel to be provided for the child to advance appropriately toward attaining annual goals, be involved and progress in the general education curriculum, participate in extracurricular and nonacademic activities, and be educated and participate with other disabled and nondisabled children; (V) an explanation of the extent, if any, to which the child will not participate with nondisabled children in the regular class and activities; (VI) a statement of any individual appropriate accommodations necessary to measure academic achievement and functional performance on State and districtwide assessments consistent with section 1412(a)(16)(A), and if the IEP Team determines the child shall take an alternate assessment on a particular State or districtwide assessment of student achievement, a statement of why the child cannot participate in the regular assessment and why the particular alternate assessment selected is appropriate; oa:hasSelector.oa:exact: (ii) Excusal

A member of the IEP Team may be excused from attending an IEP meeting, in whole or in part, when the meeting involves a modification to or discussion of the member’s area of the curriculum or related services, if—

(I) the parent and the local educational agency consent to the excusal; and

(II) the member submits, in writing to the parent and the IEP Team, input into the development of the IEP prior to the meeting.
